concerns.text: Task T001 is tagged `[P]` (parallel‑safe) but it modifies core entry‑point scripts that are required by many downstream tasks (e.g., T003, T004, T006). Running it in parallel could race with consumers that import those scripts, violating the parallel‑safety guarantee.
Task T002 is also marked `[P]` yet it produces the synthetic dataset consumed by T003‑T008. Parallel execution with any consumer would lead to missing inputs, so the `[P]` tag is unsafe.

Task T006 runs the full synthetic pipeline and validates all artifacts. It depends on the successful completion of T001‑T005, so marking it `[P]` is incorrect; it cannot safely run in parallel with its producers.

Task T009 validates statistical machinery on null and effect‑injected data and relies on the full analysis pipeline (T004‑T008). The `[P]` tag is unsafe because it consumes outputs that must be produced first.
Task T010 records runtime and memory usage after the entire pipeline finishes; it must run after all prior stages. The `[P]` tag is therefore inaccurate.
Task T011 aggregates results from many previous tasks. It cannot be parallel‑safe; the `[P]` tag should be removed.
Task T012 generates figures that depend on the aggregated results (T011). Marking it `[P]` is unsafe.
Task T013 writes the manuscript draft using all prior artifacts; it must run after T011‑T012. The `[P]` tag is inappropriate.

Task T014 (real‑data ingestion stub) is placed after tasks that may consume its output (e.g., T003 preprocessing, T004 connectivity). In a real‑data run this creates a consumer‑before‑producer ordering violation. The stub should be defined before any consumer tasks or the plan should clearly isolate synthetic‑only paths.
